transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Evelyn Brooks (Head of ML - Starlight), Carlos Mendes (Platform Eng - Starlight), Priya Shah (CPO - Starlight)
Shared artifacts: QBR deck: https://redwood.ai/qbr/starlight-2026-07.pdf, usage spreadsheet link in CRM, benchmark plan doc (to be shared)

Summary: quick review of usage, cost drivers (embeddings), two incidents in June (failover/latency spike), and discussion of Dedicated pool for heavy embedding routes; security questions and next steps captured.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining the QBR. quick check — is this still a good time?
[00:05] Evelyn Brooks: Yep, all good. We got the calendar invite, thanks.
[00:10] Maya Chen: Great. I'll run through the usage slide first and then Liam will jump into performance and dedicated options. if we run out of time we'll capture next steps.
[00:20] Liam Patel: Hey team. so the big signal from your traffic is the 2x increase in embedding requests for the knowledge search flows, mostly last quarter. that's driving token counts up and cost. we've attached a per-route cost breakout in the spreadsheet.
[00:30] Carlos Mendes: ya, the search embeddings ramped up after the release of the semantic product in May. interestingly the per-request latency is fine, but cold-starts and peak tail latency got worse at 95th.
[00:40] Liam Patel: that matches what we saw — your 95th went from ~260ms to ~420ms on hosted during peak. two incidents noted in June where a regional outage plus a fallback caused an additional 800ms delay for some traffic.
[00:55] Evelyn Brooks: right, the June 11th incident — we saw increased error rates during the deploy window. are those in the incident log?
[01:05] Maya Chen: yes, we captured both events in the incident report in the deck. the first was an autoscaler misconfiguration; the other was a model rollout where the KV cache warmup didn't happen fast enough. sometimes the transcript(s) will say KV cash or KV cache, pardon the auto transcribe.
[01:20] Priya Shah: quick question on costs — is the embedding model itself the main driver or is it tokenization + re-ranking?
[01:30] Liam Patel: mostly embeddings. you run a lot of short embeddings so per-request overhead matters; re-ranking also contributes when you do multiple rounds. our Optimize recommendations are to batch embeddings where possible and enable prefix cache for repeated texts. also consider a smaller embedding model for high-volume inferences.
[01:45] Carlos Mendes: we looked into batching but worried about latency for interactive flows. what's the tradeoff?
[01:55] Liam Patel: it's the usual latency vs cost tradeoff. for non-interactive batch offline jobs, batching aggressively reduces cost. for interactive routes you can use small batching windows and Redwood's continuous batching to keep tail latencies low. we can run an experiment on Dedicated where you get predictable throughput and smaller tail latency.
[02:15] Evelyn Brooks: can you clarify Dedicated — is that the same as Redwood Dedicated or the private deploy? i've seen "Redwood Dedicate" in some notes.
[02:25] Maya Chen: yes sorry auto notes sometimes drop the D — it's Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and predictable SLOs; Private is for VPC/on-prem installs with control plane options.
[02:35] Priya Shah: security — we still need detailed KMS and audit log info. the security team flagged SSO and SAML configuration questions.
[02:45] Liam Patel: we'll share the SOC2 package and an infra diagram. for KMS we support customer-managed keys (we call out HSM/KMS integrations in the docs). for SSO we support SAML SSO and OIDC, role-based access (RBAC), and detailed audit logs with per-route traces. i'll attach the security docs.
[03:05] Carlos Mendes: will Dedicated have separate network controls? we need VPC peering for the Dedicated hosts and the option for private egress.
[03:15] Maya Chen: Dedicated can be deployed in a private subnet with peering; we also offer a Private deployment if you need complete control or air-gapped setups. we'll include the network topology in the infra diagram.
[03:30] Liam Patel: about reliability, we've implemented more aggressive warmup for KV cache and improved canary rollout defaults to avoid the rollout-induced latency spikes. for your org, enabling automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions would have prevented the second incident.
[03:50] Evelyn Brooks: nice — can you also give guidance on quantization? we saw CPU footprints drop significantly in internal tests.
[03:58] Liam Patel: absolutely. quantized variants (8-bit or 4-bit depending on model) reduce memory and cost but can affect generation quality. our Optimize tool suggests candidate quant profiles per-model and per-workload. for embedding-only routes, quantization often works well. we'll include model-specific recommendations.
[04:15] Priya Shah: product roadmap alignment — we want to know upcoming features that affect cost controls and observability.
[04:25] Maya Chen: roadmap items relevant to you: improved per-token cost attribution, route-level caching hints, and enhanced batcher config UI within Redwood Console. also we're shipping a feature to surface regression alerts tied to prompt sets so you can detect quality drops after a model rollout.
[04:40] Carlos Mendes: can we get a sample config for batching per-route and a recommended autoscaler profile?
[04:50] Liam Patel: yes that'll be in the benchmark plan. we'll propose default autoscaler settings and a test harness so you can run with your traffic shape.
[05:05] Evelyn Brooks: one more thing — is there any work we should be doing on our side to prepare for Dedicated? like config changes or code swaps?
[05:15] Maya Chen: minimal — mostly traffic routing changes to pin high-volume routes to the Dedicated endpoint. we'll provide routing examples, model pinning config, and a rollout checklist. some teams also split read-only vs write routes to different pools.
[05:30] Priya Shah: ok perfect. on procurement timeline — we're aiming for an internal decision by end of July. so that aligns with a pilot in August if we go Dedicated.
[05:40] Maya Chen: sounds good. we'll target the benchmark in mid-July and pricing by next week.
[05:50] Liam Patel: quick note — we noticed one micro-pattern: repeated near-duplicate queries that could be cached at the prefix level. enabling prefix/KV caching will reduce token calls significantly.
[06:05] Carlos Mendes: we'll extract the top 200 queries and send them over, should help identify cacheable prefixes.
[06:15] Evelyn Brooks: anything else?
[06:20] Maya Chen: let's capture next steps. i'll send the QBR deck and usage spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow. Liam will share the benchmark plan and SOC2 docs early next week. customer to send traffic samples and security contact.
[06:35] Priya Shah: thanks all, appreciate the recommendations.
[06:40] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in CRM with links and action items.
[06:45] END

Notes about transcript: ASR imperfections noted (product names sometimes truncated, punctuation off). Speaker labels captured from calendar invite mostly, a couple of lines attributed generically in auto-transcribe.
